Subject: Amaya: Data retention & deletion SLA follow-up

Hi Daniel / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned on data retention and deletion expectations: 

1) SOC 2 / HIPAA: you asked about our audit posture — Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II; we also support HIPAA workflows and can sign a BAA.
2) Deletion SLA: for customer-managed data (user profiles, prompt inputs, outputs) we can confirm logical deletion from primary stores within 7 calendar days after a validated request.
3) Backups & snapshots: backups are immutable snapshots stored in our object store with lifecycle policies. Snapshots are retained for 30 days by default; full physical purge from backup media can take up to 90 days due to snapshot chaining and replication — we cover this in the retention policy.
4) Logs: application/tracing logs are retained 90 days by default; we can propose shorter/longer windows per contract.
5) Encryption & keys: data encrypted at rest with AES-256; customers can bring their own keys (KMS). If you request key destruction, that accelerates logical inaccessibility but we’ll follow the BAA/regulatory handling for recoverability windows.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short summary from engineering and the security questionnaire you requested.

Next steps:
- Daniel / Priya: confirm if 7/30/90 (logical deletion / snapshot retention / physical purge) works for Amaya or if you need tighter SLAs.
- I’ll loop in Neha & Rishi to complete the vendor questionnaire and provide the SOC 2 evidence pack and BAA template.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — that recap is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side before we escalate to security/legal: 

- For the 7-day logical deletion SLA: does that include derived embeddings and any cached KV data used for inference? We have strict requirements that embeddings be removed on deletion requests.
- Backups: Amaya’s compliance team prefers a maximum 60-day snapshot retention. Is there flexibility to change the default from 30 to 60 and still provide a defined physical purge window (we’d prefer under 120 days).
- Logs: Are audit logs (who accessed what) retained differently from application tracing logs? We need at least 12 months of audit logs for certain compliance traces.

Also — we’re ready to start the vendor security questionnaire; please confirm who on your security team we should expect to see answers from and an expected turnaround time.

Thanks,
Daniel

Hi Daniel — good questions. Short answers here, and I’ve asked Neha and Rishi to provide the technical evidence on the items that need deeper detail.

- Embeddings / KV cache: Yes — embeddings and cached KV state are treated as customer data. Our deletion request flow removes these artefacts from hot stores within the 7-day SLA. For caches and model-level artifacts, we provide confirmation when the purge job completes.

- Backups & retention flexibility: We can change the default snapshot retention to 60 days for Amaya as part of a contract addendum. Physical purge from replicated backups will be contractually scoped; our standard max is 90 days but we can extend to 120 days if needed. We’ll document the exact lifecycle rules (object storage lifecycle + snapshot chain behavior) in the SOW.

- Audit logs vs tracing: Audit logs (authentication/authorization/access events) are routed to a separate, tamper-evident log store and retained 12 months by default for enterprise customers. Tracing/debug logs follow the 90-day default unless otherwise configured. If you require longer retention for audit logs we can include that in the contract.

- SOC 2 / BAA / evidence: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II most recently in Feb 2027; we can provide the report under NDA. We have a standard BAA template that Neha will share. Expected turnaround for the vendor questionnaire: initial pass within 3 business days from our security team, full evidence pack within ~7-10 business days (subject to NDA).

I’ve attached the redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf that outlines the lifecycle and suggested contract language.

If these answers look reasonable, I’ll get Neha/Rishi to complete the questionnaire and we’ll send the SOC 2 NDA link.

Best,
Marissa
